chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: Lunceford's books left on the train
summary: The band played the whole Washington show from memory after the music books stayed on the baggage car.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: When we got -- we're going to Washington, we played Trenton, that's when they left the books on the train and we had to play the whole two shows without music.
Mr. Lunceford say, "Don't worry about him, because yall been playing the music. He knows. Yall been playing it all your life."
How were the books left on the train? This was a Pullman that he had. (inaudible) --
The books were on one side of the baggage car and the guy didn't turn his back to pull the rest of them.
All the stuff was probably stacked on the side. And the books were just -- you know, the two big trunks were on that side.
And he didn't turn around to pull the books out and the train pulled off (inaudible) -- and the books went on to --
Well we were going to Washington anyway to play the theater. And we got --
Well we could play. They had enough music. We played that show without any music, man. Played the whole show.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Everybody did their thing. It was a show, that place. That was a great band. That was really a great band.
